inline_comments.comment:
The background color `'#ffffde'` and the border `'1px solid #333'` on the next line are hardcoded light-theme values that will not adapt to dark or custom themes. The CSS in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/flowchart/styles.ts` already defines `div.mermaidTooltip` with theme variables (`tertiaryColor` for background, `border2` for the border), but that rule is SVG-scoped and never reaches the body-level `<div>`. This PR was a good opportunity to read those values from `getConfig().themeVariables` instead:
```ts
const { tertiaryColor, border2 } = getConfig().themeVariables ?? {};
tooltipElem
  .style('background', tertiaryColor ?? '#ffffde')
  .style('border', `1px solid ${border2 ?? '#333'}`)
```
Hardcoding hex literals here means users on dark or custom themes will always see a light-yellow tooltip with a dark border.

The selector was broadened from the specific `svg.selectAll('g.node')` to every `<g>` element that carries a `title` attribute. In a class-diagram SVG, `<g>` elements are used for many levels of structural grouping — not only top-level node containers. If an inner group (e.g., a member list row or icon group) also carries a `title` attribute, this registers overlapping `mouseover`/`mouseout` handlers for the same logical node, causing the tooltip to flicker or fire multiple times as the cursor moves within the node. `flowDb.ts` still uses the narrowed `'g.node'` selector. Identify the exact CSS class applied to top-level node containers in the class-diagram renderer and use that instead of filtering all `<g>` elements.

The guard changed from `if (title === null)` to `if (!title)`. D3's `.attr()` returns `null` when the attribute is absent and the attribute's string value otherwise. A falsy check incorrectly skips a node with `title=""` (empty string), which is a valid but semantically different case from a missing attribute. Per the project's coding standards, use strict equality: `if (title === null)`. `flowDb.ts` still uses the strict form (`if (title === null)`) on line 589, so this also creates an inconsistency between the two implementations.

`escapeHtml` is a generic HTML-escaping utility with no dependency on `ClassDB` state. Declaring it `private` on the class makes it invisible and unreusable to other diagram types (including `flowDb`) that perform the same HTML manipulation on tooltip content. It belongs in a shared location — either `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/common/common.ts` or alongside `createTooltip` in `svgDrawCommon.ts`. If the recommendation in the `.html()` comment above is adopted (use the `.text()` → `.html()` pattern), the method becomes unnecessary altogether.

general_comments.comment:
The refactoring of `flowDb.ts` is incomplete. This PR updates `flowDb.ts` to use `createTooltip()`, but the rest of its tooltip handler remains unchanged. After the PR, the two implementations diverge on multiple axes:

| Aspect | `classDb.ts` (updated) | `flowDb.ts` (unchanged) |
|---|---|---|
| Node selector | All `g` with title attr | `g.node` |
| Null guard | `!title` (falsy) | `=== null` (strict) |
| HTML encoding | custom `escapeHtml` | `.text()` → `.html()` |
| Top offset | `rect.bottom + 4` | `rect.bottom` |
| String templates | template literals | string concatenation |

If the 4 px bottom offset and other improvements are correct, they should be applied consistently to `flowDb.ts` in the same PR to prevent the two implementations from drifting further apart.

No unit or end-to-end tests were added (the PR checklist acknowledges this). The fix changes three distinct behaviors for class diagrams: the node selector, the bounding-rect retrieval (the core bug fix), and the tooltip position relative to the element. At minimum, a Cypress `imgSnapshotTest` in `cypress/integration/rendering/classDiagram.spec.js` should assert that a tooltip appears near the hovered node rather than at the document bottom, and a unit test should verify that tooltip text containing `
` and HTML special characters is rendered correctly.
